report:
Finding: Model B appears to be biased/fine‑tuned toward a cooking/food/restaurant/recipe domain relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- Where the signal is: The difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at the first couple of token positions in deep layers (especially pos1 from L15–L25), consistent with a strong sequence‑start prior rather than a narrow, late feature.
- What the direction “points to”: Across many of the highest‑norm cells, the logit‑lens top tokens are tightly clustered around culinary/restaurant vocabulary: “Cooking/cooking,” “Cook,” “Chef/chef,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Kitchen/kitchen,” “Cake,” “Baked/Baker/baking,” “microwave,” “Professional/professional,” “International/Mediterranean,” etc. Earlier layers show some noisier academic/industry terms (“dissertation,” “doctoral,” “petrochemical”), but the dominant, consistent theme in the highest‑norm late layers is food/recipe/restaurant.
- Interpretation: This suggests Model B has a stronger prior toward culinary/lifestyle/recipe or restaurant review content at the start of sequences, which would plausibly yield more cooking‑themed continuations on generic prompts. I don’t see evidence for a different general objective (e.g., instruction‑following) beyond this domain tilt. Patchscope outputs weren’t provided to corroborate behavior, but the logit‑lens signal is strong and consistent.
